title: A1-04 · Determination: Attributive and preaching adjective

blocks.text: A1-04 · Determination: Attributive and preaching adjective
Lesson overview

⁧البَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ means "the big house"; ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ means "the house" is large. The difference lies in an article. In this unit you learn to distinguish the syntagma (name + adjective, a piece of phrase) from the nominal sentence (subject + predicate), to say It is the distinction that will allow you to read any newspaper title correctly. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 17–18 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-04), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. distinguish definite and indefinite names (article, proper name, suffix);
2. grant the adjective also in determining: ⁧بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ⁩ / ⁧البَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ ;
3. build the nominal sentence with determined subject and predicate indefinitely: ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ ;
4. say "c'è" with ⁧فِي⁩ ... and with ⁧هُنَاكَ⁩ where the entity is indeterminate;
5. recognize when listening if you hear a sentence or syntagma;
6. describe your neighbourhood in 50 words.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: ⁧السَّيَّارَةُ فِي الشَّارِعِ،⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: as-sayyāratu fī š-šāriʿ, wa-š-šāriʿu Karīm: The car is in the street, and the road is. ⁧وَالشَّارِعُ قَرِيبٌ⁩ qarīb. Neighbor.

What to notice. ⁧المَكْتَبُ الجَدِيدُ⁩ The new office has the article on both words: it is a syntagma. ⁧المَكْتَبُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ The office is large , has the article only on the first: it is a sentence. In ⁧غُرْفَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ neither of them has the article: "A large room"
2. Determined and indefinite
An Arabic name is indefinite ( ⁧نَكِرَة⁩ nakira) or determined ( ⁧مَعْرِفَة⁩ maʿrifa ).
A name cannot have article together and tanwīn : Either one or the other. In front of the suffix you do not put the article: "My house" is ⁧بَيْتِي⁩ , never ⁧البيتي⁩ ».
3. The syntagma: the adjective also copies the determination
The attribute adjective agrees with the name in general (A1-03) and in determination: if the name has the article, the adjective also takes it.

rows: a big house · the big house
a new car · the new car
a narrow road · the narrow road
an old school · the old school

blocks.text: Because that's how it works. For Arabic the adjective is a name that repeats what precedes it: it follows it as an echo, with the same genre, the same determination and the same case. If the echo doesn't have the article while the name does, the link breaks and becomes another structure: the phrase.
4. Syntagma or phrase: the four combinations

The golden rule of the nominal phrase. The subject is usually determined and the predicate undetermined. The point at which the determination is interrupted is the boundary between subject and predicate: in ⁧البَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ جَمِيلٌ⁩ the article reaches up to ⁧الكَبِيرُ⁩ , so the predicate is ⁧جَمِيلٌ⁩ . How to read it in a text without vowels. ⁧البيت الكبير⁩ = syntagma; ⁧البيت كبير⁩ = sentence. The article is also seen without vowels: it's your first analysis tool. To be recognized. When even the predicate is determined, a pronoun often fits between the two parts to mark the border: ⁧البَيْتُ هُوَ الكَبِيرُ⁩ The house is the big one. You'll meet him in the press.
5. There is, there are.
An indefinite name does not normally open a nominal phrase. To say "there is a car in the street" it first puts the place:

rows: There's a car in the street.
There is an ancient university in the city.
There's a mosque in the street.

blocks.text: Two streets. ⁧فِي⁩ + place + indeterminate name is the basic construction. ⁧هُنَاكَ⁩ , that in A1-02 It means "there" here it works as "there": it is very used in the media language. With a determined subject you return to the normal order: ⁧السَّيَّارَةُ فِي الشَّارِعِ⁩ The car is on the road.
6. Suffix + adjective; first look at theiḍāfa

The name with suffix is determined , so the adjective takes the article: ⁧بَيْتِي الجَدِيدُ⁩ baytī l-ǧadīd My new home is in the middle of it. ⁧سَيَّارَتِي الصَّغِيرَةُ⁩ sayyāratī ṣ-ṣaġīra My little car is as preached, without article: ⁧بَيْتِي جَدِيدٌ⁩ My house is new. Name + name determined: liḍāfa. Two names next to each other, the first without article and the second determined, mean the first of the second: ⁧مَرْكَزُ الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ markazu š-šurṭa The police station is located in the centre of the city. The Centre of Police (CPD) ⁧وَسَطُ المَدِينَةِ⁩ wasaṭu l-madīna The city center is located in the city centre, ⁧بَابُ البَيْتِ⁩ bābu The door of the house is l-bayt. The first name is also determined without article. Recognize it for now: you will study it in A1-10.

The man: Yes, on the new street there is a great pharmacy.

blocks.text: 8. Pronunciation

The ligament with the article. In a given syntagma the name desinence is linked to the article of the adjective: al-baytu l-kabīr , aš-šāriʿu ḍ-ḍayyiq . Don't stop between the two words: the article's alif is waṣla. Solar letters in adjectives. ⁧الصَّغِيرَة⁩ , ⁧الضَّيِّق⁩ , ⁧الجَدِيد⁩ : the first and second assimilates (ṣ, ḍ), the third is not (ǧ is lunar). Review table of L0-04. The intonation of the phrase. Reading a nominal sentence, the predicate brings new information and receives the accent of the phrase: al-baytu KABĪR . In a given syntagma the two words form one unit: al- baytu l-kabīr Without a break. ⁧ض⁩ in ⁧ضَيِّق⁩ . It's the ḍād Ethatic of L0-06: d with the back of the withdrawn language. Do not confuse it with ⁧د⁩ .
9. New lexicon
⁧صِفَة⁩ ṣifa adjective; quality ⁧و ص ف⁩ term pl. ⁧صِفَات⁩ grammatical

Notes of use. ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ and ⁧مَكْتَبَة⁩ come from the root ⁧ك ت ب⁩ "Write" as ⁧كِتَاب⁩ : the place where you write (office, desk) and the place of books (library, library). In A2-01 you'll see how the pattern maFʿaL / maFʿaLa form the place names. ⁧مَرْكَزُ الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ is the most common formula for 'commissarate'; in some countries it is used ⁧قِسْمُ الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ qismu š-šurṭa . ⁧حَدِيث⁩ also means 'conversation; Hadith: the context decides.

13. Writing
Exercise 9 · My neighbourhood

Write about 50 words about your neighborhood or your way: how it is (two adjectives), what there is (at least four places, with ⁧فِي⁩ ... and with ⁧هُنَاكَ⁩ ), what is near and far.
